differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: TiKV stores data as unstructured byte arrays mapped to unique keys, offering extreme flexibility for arbitrary data structures and distributed storage.
differences.rightDesc: TiDB presents data in structured tables with defined schemas, rows, and columns, enabling complex queries and ACID transactions for relational workloads.

differences.title: 2. CONSISTENCY
differences.leftDesc: Ensures strong consistency for distributed reads/writes using Multi-Version Concurrency Control and the Raft consensus algorithm across its nodes.
differences.rightDesc: Achieves ACID compliance and strong consistency via MVCC and Raft, guaranteeing reliable transaction processing for distributed relational data.

differences.title: 3. QUERY LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: TiKV does not interpret queries directly; it serves data based on provided keys. A layer above handles query logic and translation.
differences.rightDesc: Supports standard SQL queries with a MySQL protocol endpoint, allowing seamless integration with existing applications and tools.

differences.title: 4. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: TiKV acts as the distributed storage backend, handling the physical data storage and replication for a distributed database system.
differences.rightDesc: TiDB is a complete NewSQL database system, integrating a distributed SQL layer and a distributed KV storage engine (TiKV).

differences.title: 5. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Scales out by adding more TiKV nodes to distribute storage and read/write load, ensuring high throughput and availability.
differences.rightDesc: Scales out compute and storage independently by adding nodes, designed for massive, elastic growth of both data and traffic.

differences.title: 6. USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Primarily serves as the robust, distributed storage layer for TiDB, providing the foundation for its SQL capabilities.
differences.rightDesc: Ideal for high-concurrency Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) with mixed workloads, web-scale applications, and cloud-native environments.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires a separate SQL layer for query execution, offering raw control over data but demanding more infrastructure management.
differences.rightDesc: Provides a complete, user-friendly SQL interface, simplifying database management and application development significantly.
